subject: On-prem Kubernetes deployment: node pools, storage & network checklist

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes deployment: node pools, storage & network checklist

Hi Samantha — attaching a starter spec and a simple network diagram (see attachments). High level answers below; we can iterate once your infra team reviews.

Quick summary (see attached spreadsheet for values we used to estimate):
- Node pools: control-plane (3 x m5a.xlarge equivalent), inference workers (variable: dedicated G4/G5 or on-prem GPU nodes), inference CPU workers (2-4 x m5.xlarge for API frontends), infra/system pool (2 x m5.large: monitoring, logging, operator).
- Storage: Recommend CSI with per-namespace PVs on NFS for logs and a high-performance block storage class (iSCSI/LVM or local NVMe backed) for model artifacts/weights. Snapshotting for model releases; retention policy configurable.
- Networking: Private VPC-style CIDR (e.g., 10.40.0.0/16), dedicated subnets per node-pool, ingress LB for public API (optional), mandatory egress proxy for outbound controls. Needed ports: 443 for API, 2379-2380 for etcd (cluster-internal), kube-apiserver (6443), and SSH restricted to jump hosts.
- Audit & logging: Control plane audit logs streamed to your SIEM (syslog/forwarder), operator actions logged to an append-only store; we can supply log schema and retention templates for SOC2.

Next step: Can your team share a preferred CIDR, existing storage backend details (NFS/iSCSI/ceph/NetApp), and whether GPUs will be physically colocated or accessed via shared nodes?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes deployment: node pools, storage & network checklist

Adding sizing guidance from ops perspective:
- Inference worker sizing: assume 1 GPU per model-serving pod; recommend a mix of 8 GPU nodes for initial pilot (A100 or equivalent) and autoscale groups for CPU-bound tasks. If you expect bursty traffic, leave room for a 20% buffer in GPU capacity.
- Node pool taints/tolerations: GPU pool should be tainted to avoid accidental scheduling. Use a dedicated node selector label (redwood=inference-gpu).
- PVCs: Use StorageClass with ReclaimPolicy: Retain for model artifacts, Delete for ephemeral caches. Enable dynamic provisioning if your backend supports it.

I'll also include a short checklist for procurement to place in the spec.

- Stephanie
Manager, Customer Engineering
From: Samantha Perez <samantha.perez@acme-corp.com>

Thanks Dev and Stephanie — helpful. A few clarifying points from infra:
- CIDR: we can allocate 10.200.0.0/16 for the Redwood cluster.
- Storage backend: we have NetApp ONTAP (iSCSI + NFS), and a couple of racks with local NVMe that can be used for high-perf workloads.
- GPUs: we will provide 4 A100 nodes initially, and can add more if needed.
- Compliance: for SOC2 we need an exporter that pushes audit logs to our Splunk instance over TLS; can Redwood run the forwarder as a DaemonSet?

Samantha
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem Kubernetes deployment: node pools, storage & network checklist

Hi Samantha — good info. A few concrete notes from engineering:
- NetApp + NFS is fine for model artifacts and artifacts that don't need very low latency. For model weights we prefer local NVMe-backed PVs mounted via CSI-driver-local or LVM provisioner for <5ms latency. We'll include a fallback to a blob-backed cache for large models to limit memory usage.
- DaemonSet for a Splunk forwarder is standard — we will provide a small Helm chart and values to configure TLS + auth token rotation.
- Etcd: recommend isolated control-plane network and backup snapshot schedule (daily + weekly retention). We'll run the Redwood control plane in a private namespace; operator access is RBAC-restricted and we can provide a read-only view for your auditors.
- Backup targets: S3-compatible endpoint (minio or on-prem object) for snapshots; please confirm if an internal S3 endpoint exists or we should provision MinIO.

I'll turn the above into the network/ops section of the attached spec and flag required firewall rules.

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Runtime
